findings.reason: the done-when requires the mapping demonstrated on one running process, and with this command it cannot be; the plan must name `source_code_identity` (reckon/checkout_trust.py:388) or the `ls-tree HEAD reckon skills` + catalogue composition as the comparison, or the investigating node either reports a false "uncommitted code" verdict or spends its budget on a mismatch it cannot resolve.
findings.text: the Why says the admit service's `code_stamp` (01863fb71f) "is compared against the reckon tree of a commit, not against a commit: `git rev-parse <commit>:reckon` must equal it", but 01863fb71f is the composed reload tree of `reckon` + `skills` + the docs catalogue blob (`git cat-file -p 01863fb71f` prints three entries: docs 4781e2f6, reckon b339396f, skills 9369d6f4), while `git rev-parse HEAD:reckon` is b339396f on the reviewed base — the inner subtree, never the stamp; `checkout_trust._committed_reload_tree` composes the stamp from `git ls-tree HEAD reckon skills` plus the catalogue, so a node running the prescribed command compares a 40-char subtree id against a different object and finds no commit for any revision, reinstating exactly the "matched no commit" false negative §14 exists to correct
